1.why: Recovery verify requires the record’s sessionId to match the caller’s session and validates the token hash before advancing, so the code is bound to the requesting user/session.

2.why: A reset code is stored only on one RecoveryRecord tied to sessionId; another user/session fails the sessionId and stage checks, so the same code does not work for others.

3.why: Password reset only updates accountPasswordHash and the current session; other entries in the sessions Map are never invalidated.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, but the code does not explicitly pin the latest TLS version.

5.why: Reset tokens and passwords are protected with bcrypt via Bun.password.hash; other in-memory user/session fields are not encrypted at rest.

6.why: There is no real email sender; the recovery API uses a generic anti-enumeration message, though testToken is returned for demo delivery simulation.

7.why: Inputs pass through cleanText, validIdentifier, and validPassword, which bound length and reject control characters and angle brackets.

8.why: Navigation uses a fixed validRoutes allowlist and API next paths are internal (e.g. /password); no user-controlled external redirects exist.

9.why: No email HTML templates consume user input; client rendering escapes dynamic text with esc() and CSP nonces block inline script injection.

10.why: Error JSON is generic and stack traces are swallowed, but testToken/testMfaCode are returned and written into the on-page logs area.

11.why: Runtime password storage uses bcrypt, yet MFA_TEST_CODE and the initial password string are hardcoded in source.

12.why: DEMO_ACCOUNT_IDENTIFIER helena@hospital.test with password Welcome!2025Heart is accepted as working default demo credentials.

13.why: Login, recovery-request, recovery-verify, and MFA paths apply attempt counters and temporary lockouts (e.g. 5 failures → LOCK_TIME_MS).

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same ‘if the details match’ success message, and login failures use a single non-enumerating error string.

15.why: Codes are randomBytes(32) base64url tokens, bcrypt-hashed, single-use, short-lived, and bound to the requester’s recovery record/session.
